reconcile.connective: Defenders read Genesis 2 not as a rival timeline but as the sixth day's sequence spelled out, with Eve's making narrated in order after Adam's.

discrepancy.connective: Source critics, classically Julius Wellhausen, assign Genesis 1 to the Priestly writer and Genesis 2 to the Yahwist, arguing the two creation reports cannot be reconciled into one sequence — in P the pair is made together, in J the woman is fashioned separately and last.

skeptic.name: Julius Wellhausen
skeptic.work: Prolegomena to the History of Israel
skeptic.attribution: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (Eng. trans. 1885; German 1878/1883)

excerpts.excerpt_text: In Gen 1:27 the creation of the woman is linked with that of the man; but here the order of sequence is given, because the creation of the woman formed a chronological incident in the history of the human race, which commences with the creation of Adam. The circumstance that in Gen 2:19 the formation of the beasts and birds is connected with the creation of Adam by the imperf. c. ו consec., constitutes to objection to the plan of creation given in Gen 1.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly addresses the timing/sequence discrepancy: Gen 1:27 makes man and woman together, Gen 2 gives the order, and K&D argue this difference of presentation is no objection to the Gen 1 plan. Anchor-block note; on-tension sentences pulled from within the block.

pd_work.resource: Keil & Delitzsch, Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament (1861-75), on Genesis 2:18-22
pd_work.author: Keil & Delitzsch
pd_work.note: Keil & Delitzsch treat this exact discrepancy directly, arguing the Genesis 2 order of sequence (woman formed after Adam and the animals) is no objection to the plan of creation in Genesis 1, where male and female are made together on the sixth day.

link.title: GotQuestions: Why weren't Adam and Eve created at the same time (Genesis 2)?
link.note: Live apologetic treatment keyed to this row's man/woman-ordering tension: why the woman was made separately and after Adam (Genesis 2:18-22) rather than together with him as in Genesis 1:27.
